summary: Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a professor at Sichuan University around 1987 and was attested as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.

Bingtao Ma specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University by 2008 and completed his PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha studied philosophy at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, then earned an A.M. and Ph.D. from Harvard. He was Director of the Anthropological Survey of India and the Bihar Tribal Research Institute.

Birgit Kellner, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earned her doctorate from Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. She has held posts at the University of Vienna, Heidelberg University, and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Biscoe Hale Wortham was an Indology scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge in 1863 and completed a B.A. at Trinity College, Oxford between 1863 and 1868.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu worked in Indology and archaeology after studying under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. Around 1920 to 1950, he headed the Government Museum Jodhpur, Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and Sumer Public Library's Archaeological Department.
Biswajit Biswas is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and was attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Biswanath Banerjee, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studied under doctoral supervisor Helmut Hoffmann around 1957–1959. He was on the faculty at Visva-Bharati University (1967–1991) and served as president of The Asiatic Society.
Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Harvard University (2002–2009) and was appointed professor at the University of Lausanne in 2013.

Blanche Christine Olschak was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Graz (~1933–1937). In 1946, she studied under Constantin Régamey and Thupten Wangyal.
Bo Jiang specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Uppsala University (~1957–1973) under Stig Wikander and Henrik Samuel Nyberg, later serving as professor emeritus at Uppsala (~1987–2003).
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Dongguk University, where his posts were attested in 2004 and 2015. He also taught Silwon Suk.
Bohumil Sládeček was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý by 1918.

Bojan Čop was a linguist specializing in Indo-European and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Ljubljana under Karel Oštir, earning his PhD there and later serving as full professor from 1972 to 1990.
Bokar Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who studied under Kalu Rinpoche between 1959 and 1989. He held a post at Bokar Monastery from around 1984 to 2004.
Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. He held faculty posts at Florida International University in 1991–1992 and in 2012 as professor of philosophy.

Borayin Larios studied at the University of Freiburg and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Vienna, the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and served as department head at the French Institute of Pondicherry (2023–2024).

Boris Aleksandrovich Larin studied linguistics and Indology at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1910–1914). He served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1922, including as chair of Slavonic Philology (1962–1964).
